# Laws pass Parliament to deliver two new public holidays for WA

Legislation to give Western Australians two additional public holidays has passed Parliament.


- New laws give WA two new public holidays from
2028 – Show Day and Easter Saturday – while dates for three other public
holidays will be moved
- Changes will align WA's public holidays with
other states, improving productivity
- Cook Labor Government ensuring WA remains the
best place in the world to live, do business and raise a family

Legislation to give Western
Australians two additional public holidays has passed Parliament.

The changes will see the dates
of two existing public holidays, Labour Day and the King's Birthday, moved to
better align Western Australia with other states and territories and support
economic activity and productivity.

WA Day will also move to
November, giving Western Australians a break ahead of the Christmas season and
ensuring celebrations can be enjoyed outside of winter.

Two new public holidays, Easter
Saturday and Show Day, will provide certainty for Western Australians and
ensure workers are paid appropriately when working on those public holidays.

The changes were developed
following extensive community consultation, including more than 10,000
submissions from businesses, not-for-profit organisations, peak bodies, unions
and members of the broader community.

With the legislation now
passed, a two-year implementation period will allow businesses, organisations,
governments and the broader WA community to prepare for the new public holiday
calendar commencing in 2028.

This transition period will
provide time to make the necessary administrative and operational arrangements
ahead of the changes taking effect.

**Comments attributed to**
**Premier Roger Cook:**

"My government has modernised
WA's public holiday calendar which will be better suited to modern life in WA,
following clear, broad support from the Western Australian community.

"We're creating two new public
holidays, Easter Saturday and Show Day, and aligning three other public
holidays with other States to help boost productivity.

"With this legislation now
passed, Western Australians can look forward to two additional public holidays
and a modernised public holiday calendar from 2028."
